title: GSC engine builtin catalogue
description: One game's engine builtins (functions and methods the VM resolves by name or hash), as extracted from the game's executable. Validates builtins/<engine-id>.toml after TOML parsing. Facts only: names, hashes, arities, parameter types and how each was measured; no documentation text.

source.description: Where the facts come from, e.g. "extracted from game executable".

hash_family.description: gsc_hash family id of the `hash` field (t7.canon, t8.fnv64...).

extraction.description: How the catalogue was produced: tool, executable identity, entry layout, the lookups and their tables.

executable_sp.description: The single-player executable merged into the catalogue (IW5, S1, H1).

modes.description: The game modes whose executables were read, each with its executable's file name (one executable may run several modes: the T4/T5 campaign executable runs zombies, the S1 multiplayer one Exo Zombies). An entry's `modes` is a subset of these keys. A mode absent here was not read (an encrypted executable): tools cannot narrow its scripts' builtins. Written by tools/re/modes.py.

merge.description: The single-player merge: entries only the SP executable has, and how many shared entries measured the same arity in both.

arity_source.description: How min_args/max_args were measured for the whole catalogue (an entry's own arity_source overrides it).

vm_globals.description: Where the VM keeps its parameter count (scrVmPub.outparamcount) and stack top, as the IW extraction found them. base image: RVAs of globals; base context: offsets in the VM context structure the handlers receive (IW8, JUP).

corpus_second_measure.description: The corpus pass applied to the arities (tools/re/calibrate.py): corpus, date of the pass and what it changed.

corpus_type_measure.description: The corpus pass that measured argument types (tools/re/types_corpus.py): call sites, files, entries given a corpus_param_types and the threshold.

intrinsic.description: Names the compiler turns into one VM opcode (isdefined, vectorscale, gettime...): no lookup resolves them, so a call site is not a table builtin, even where a table also holds the name. Tools read this list, not the profile's opcode_builtins, to know these names and their arity.

also_builtin.description: Lookups (gsc_function...) whose tables also hold the name's hash.

corpus_args.description: Argument counts seen at the corpus call sites.

arity_source.description: Where min_args/max_args come from (the corpus call sites: the compiler checks an intrinsic's count, so the shipped scripts only hold accepted counts).

coverage.description: Whether the catalogue holds every builtin the game's scripts can call. complete = false when an executable of the game was not extracted (a mode's scripts may call builtins it lacks) or entries have neither a name nor a hash: tools then cannot call a missing name unknown (gruff check turns B001 off). Absent: complete.

complete_modes.description: With complete = false: the game modes whose executables were all read and whose entries are all named, so a name missing from the catalogue is unknown to the engine in scripts of these modes (gruff check keeps B001 on for them).

builtin.description: One table entry. Engines that key their tables by hash (T7+, JUP) always give `hash`; engines whose tables point at the name string (T4-T6, IW1, IW3) give `name` with name_source "executable"; the IW registration builds give the registration `id` (IW5+) or the entry's `index` (IW4), and a name when one is known.

name.description: Lower-case name; present only when a string hashing to `hash` is known, or when the table stores the string itself.

name_source.description: Where the name string came from; the hash match is the proof. executable: the table entry points at the name string (no hash involved). gsc-tool: gsc-tool's id or hash table (GPL-3.0), matched by id or hash; iw5-handler-match: the one IW5 handler of the same code shape and arity, named from gsc-tool. Both make the entry GPL-3.0-only.

dev_only.description: Developer builtin: T7+ type_flags 1 (the linker's 'Dev only calls must be wrapped in a devblock'); T4-T6 the table's developer flag.

arity_source.description: How min_args/max_args were measured when the table does not store them (e.g. T4/T5: handler emulation with N parameters).

table.description: Engine table holding the entry, when a lookup has several (informative).

max_args.description: variadic_max when unbounded; -1 only with arity_unchecked or arity_unknown.

arity_unchecked.description: The entry stores -1/-1 (0xFFFFFFFF) for min and max: no arity recorded.

type_flags.description: The entry's type word as the engine's lookup returns it. T7: 1 on debug builtins (line, print3d, assert...: dev-only, the linker's 'Dev only calls must be wrapped in a devblock'), 2 on the __protected__ names.

type_field.description: Raw type word of the table entry, when the lookup does not return it.

param_types.description: Per index, the type(s) of the accessor the handler used ('?' not read). Best effort: a handler run under emulation, with N = min(max, 16) parameters.

shadowed.description: The same hash sits in an earlier table of the same lookup: the engine never returns this entry.

license.description: The entry's licence when it differs from the file's: GPL-3.0-only exactly when the name comes from gsc-tool (name_source gsc-tool or iw5-handler-match). Absent: the file's licence.

id.description: IW5+: the id the engine registers the handler under (the bytecode's builtin reference).

index.description: IW4: the entry's position in its registration order (no id).

max_checked.description: The handler rejects more than max_args (an explicit usage check, or JUP's table bound). false: extra arguments are ignored, so only min_args is a rule.

arity_mode.description: How the IW handler runs measured the arity: strict (script errors unwind), strict+state (after setting the state the handler checks first), lenient (errors return; the baseline errors subtracted), table (JUP: the entry's u8 min/max, handler runs as the second measure).

arity_unknown.description: No trusted arity: no handler run passed, the table stores none, or the corpus contradicts the measure (corpus_arity = "unknown"). min_args/max_args are then -1, or the discarded measure, and tools never check the argument count.

executables.description: The executables whose tables hold the entry (IW games with a merged SP executable).

modes.description: The game modes whose executables hold the entry, when that is not every mode of [extraction] `modes` (absent: every mode read, or the split is unknown). Scripts of a mode can call only the entries of that mode (tools/re/modes.py, from one extraction per executable).

mode_args.description: Each mode's [min_args, max_args] as its executable's table stores it, when the executables holding the entry disagree (T6: linker-checked). Scripts of a mode are checked against their mode's pair; min_args/max_args stay the catalogue's, for scripts of no known mode.

measured_args.description: The extraction's own [min, max] when the corpus pass changed min_args/max_args or set arity_unknown.

corpus_arg_types.description: The corpus measure of the parameter types (tools/re/types_corpus.py, gruff types): per argument index, how many call sites of the game's own scripts pass each inferred type (literals, known builtin results, local flow, script parameters to a fixpoint); unknown = not determinable from the scripts. Independent of param_types, which it never changes.

corpus_param_types.description: Per index, the type derived from corpus_arg_types when consistent: at least 5 typed sites (unknown and undefined left out, bool counted as int) and one type at 95% or more; int and float mixed give number, string and hash mixed hash|string; '?' otherwise. Tools show it where param_types gives no type; disagreements with param_types are listed in tools/re/reports/types_<game>.md.

corpus_arity.description: The corpus second measure contradicted the extraction (tools/re/calibrate.py): unknown = the measure is discarded (arity_unknown), widened = min/max now include the argument counts the game's own scripts use. The evidence line says where.
